joint.name: Lower back
joint.subtitle: Lumbar spine and pelvis, seen from behind

lombalgie.name: Non-specific low back pain
lombalgie.whatYouFeel: Pain in the lower back, sometimes in the buttock, that changes with positions and movements.
lombalgie.whatHappens: In nine cases out of ten, no precise injury explains the pain. The back remains strong and movement is part of the treatment.
lombalgie.warning: Emergency (112 or your local number) without waiting: difficulty passing urine or leaks, loss of bowel control, numbness between the legs, weakness spreading to one or both legs. See a doctor promptly if you have a fever, after a fall or a blow, with a history of cancer, unexplained weight loss, pain that does not ease with rest or at night, or a first episode of back pain after 50.

lumbago.name: Acute low back pain
lumbago.whatYouFeel: Sudden band of pain across the lower back, back locked, leaning to one side, for a few days.
lumbago.whatHappens: The muscles alongside the spine contract strongly and block movement. The episode usually heals in less than two weeks.
lumbago.whoIsAffected: Adults aged 30 to 50, after an effort or an awkward movement, sometimes for no reason.
lumbago.warning: Pain running below the knee with loss of strength: see a doctor promptly. Emergency (112 or your local number) if you have difficulty passing urine, lose bowel control or feel numbness between the legs. Also see a doctor if the pain has not eased at all after a week.

sciatique.name: Sciatica from a disc herniation
sciatique.whatYouFeel: Pain from the buttock to the back of the thigh, the calf and the foot, often stronger than the back pain, worse when sitting and when coughing.
sciatique.whatHappens: The L4-L5 or L5-S1 disc bulges backwards and irritates a root of the sciatic nerve. In most cases the herniation shrinks on its own.
sciatique.warning: Emergency (112 or your local number): difficulty passing urine or leaks, loss of bowel control, numbness between the legs, pain in both legs, foot drop or weakness that gets worse. Also see a doctor if the pain stays unbearable despite painkillers.

canal.name: Lumbar spinal stenosis
canal.whatYouFeel: Pain, heaviness or pins and needles in both legs when walking, which force you to stop and ease when sitting or leaning forward.
canal.whatHappens: The canal the nerve roots run through narrows with arthritis. It opens up when the back rounds, hence the relief when leaning forward.
canal.warning: Emergency (112 or your local number): difficulty passing urine or leaks, numbness between the legs, legs giving way. See a doctor if your walking distance shrinks week after week. If calf pain goes away as soon as you stop and stand still, without sitting or leaning, tell your doctor: the arteries may be involved.

disco.name: Degenerative disc disease
disco.whatYouFeel: Band of pain in the middle of the lower back, worse after sitting for long and leaning forward, stiffness on getting up.
disco.whatHappens: With age, discs lose a little water and height, just as hair turns grey. These scan findings are just as common in people without pain. They do not mean the back is fragile: moving and getting stronger remains the treatment.
disco.whoIsAffected: Over 40. At 50, about eight in ten people without back pain show this kind of finding.
disco.warning: Night pain that wakes you, or morning stiffness lasting more than an hour: see a doctor.

facettes.name: Facet joint osteoarthritis
facettes.whatYouFeel: Pain on one side of the lower back when arching, when standing for long, eased by sitting or leaning forward.
facettes.whatHappens: Small joints link the vertebrae at the back. They wear and become painful when the back arches.
facettes.warning: Pain running down both legs when walking: see a doctor.

si.name: Sacroiliac joint pain
si.commonName: Pain at the top of one buttock
si.whatYouFeel: Pain below the belt line, on one side, above the buttock, when turning over in bed or climbing stairs.
si.whatHappens: The sacroiliac joint links the sacrum to the pelvic bone. Strong ligaments hold it, but it can become irritated.
si.whoIsAffected: During or after pregnancy, after a fall onto the buttocks, sometimes with no clear cause.
si.warning: Waking in the second half of the night and morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes, before 45: see a doctor, inflammatory arthritis is possible. Severe night pain, fever or weight loss: see a doctor promptly.

tassement.name: Vertebral compression fracture
tassement.whatYouFeel: Sudden pain in the middle of the back or the upper lower back after minimal effort, worse standing, eased lying down.
tassement.whatHappens: The body of a vertebra weakened by osteoporosis collapses, most often where the mid back meets the lower back.
tassement.whoIsAffected: Over 60, especially women, with osteoporosis, long-term cortisone treatment or a previous fracture.
tassement.warning: Sudden back pain after 60, even without a fall: see a doctor within days. An X-ray confirms it, and osteoporosis can be treated. In the meantime, avoid carrying loads and bending forward with a rounded back. Also see a doctor if you have a history of cancer. Emergency (112 or your local number) if the legs weaken or you have bladder problems.

listhesis.name: Spondylolisthesis
listhesis.whatYouFeel: Band of pain across the lower back when arching, tight muscles at the back of the thigh.
listhesis.whatHappens: A crack in the back arch of L5, or wear of the joints, lets the vertebra slide forward over the one below.
listhesis.whoIsAffected: Teenage athletes (gymnastics, diving), or over 50 through arthritis.
listhesis.warning: A teenage athlete with pain when arching for more than two weeks: see a doctor and pause sports that arch the back (gymnastics, dance, diving, tennis serve), a stress fracture of the vertebra is possible. Pins and needles or weakness in the legs: see a doctor. Bladder problems: emergency (112 or your local number).

ql.name: Quadratus lumborum pain
ql.whatYouFeel: Deep pain between the last ribs and the pelvis, on one side, when leaning sideways or standing up.
ql.whatHappens: The quadratus lumborum links the ribs, the lumbar vertebrae and the pelvis. When overloaded, it stays tight and tender.
ql.whoIsAffected: Long periods of sitting, carrying loads on one side, work bent over.
ql.warning: Flank pain with fever or burning when passing urine: see a doctor, a kidney may be involved.

cruralgie.name: Femoral radiculopathy
cruralgie.commonName: Pain at the front of the thigh
cruralgie.whatYouFeel: Pain from the groin down the front of the thigh to the knee, often worse at night, sometimes weakness when climbing stairs.
cruralgie.whatHappens: An L3 or L4 root of the femoral nerve is irritated, by a disc or by arthritis.
cruralgie.warning: Knee giving way or thigh weakening: see a doctor promptly. Emergency (112 or your local number) with bladder problems or numbness between the legs. Groin pain when walking can also come from the hip: an examination tells them apart.

spa.name: Axial spondyloarthritis
spa.whatYouFeel: Pain in the buttocks and lower back in the second half of the night, morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes, better with movement.
spa.whatHappens: A long-term inflammation first affects the sacroiliac joints, then the spine. Movement relieves it, rest makes it worse.
spa.warning: This picture calls for medical advice: treatments slow the disease. Daily exercise is part of it. Red, painful eye: see a doctor the same day.

marche.name: Walking
marche.how: 10 to 30 minutes a day, at your own pace, even if the back pulls a little.
marche.videoSearch: low back pain walking advice physiotherapist

chat.name: Cat and cow
chat.how: On all fours, round then hollow the back. 10 slow repetitions.

genoux.name: Knees to chest
genoux.how: Lying down, bring one knee then the other towards the chest. 10 times each side.
genoux.videoSearch: knees to chest lower back stretch

bird.name: Bird-dog
bird.how: On all fours, extend one arm and the opposite leg. 3 sets of 8 each side.
bird.videoSearch: bird dog exercise core low back pain

bascule.name: Pelvic tilt lying down
bascule.how: Flatten the lower back then relax. 2 sets of 10.

sphinx.name: Prone extension on the forearms
sphinx.how: Lying face down, prop yourself on your forearms with the pelvis on the floor, hold 5 to 10 s. 10 times. Only continue if the leg pain lessens or moves back up towards the back. Stop if it moves further down the leg.
sphinx.videoSearch: McKenzie prone extension sphinx disc herniation

nsci.name: Sciatic nerve glide
nsci.how: Sitting on the edge of a chair, back straight. Straighten the knee while lifting the head towards the ceiling, then bend the knee while lowering the head. 10 times slowly. Pins and needles must not increase.

ncru.name: Femoral nerve glide
ncru.how: Lying on your side, heel towards the buttock then relax. 10 times slowly.

pontb.name: Glute bridge with a ball between the knees
pontb.how: Squeeze the ball as you lift. 3 sets of 10.
pontb.videoSearch: glute bridge ball between knees sacroiliac

planche.name: Forearm plank
planche.how: Body in a straight line, hold 20 to 30 s, 3 times.

lat.name: Side plank on the knees
lat.how: Resting on the forearm and knees, hold 20 s, 3 times each side.

etql.name: Side stretch
etql.how: Standing, arm above the head, lean to the opposite side. 3 times 30 s.

flex.name: Seated forward bend
flex.how: Sitting, lean forward, hands towards the floor. 10 times, gives relief with spinal stenosis.
flex.videoSearch: seated lumbar flexion spinal stenosis exercise

velo.name: Exercise bike
velo.how: Trunk leaning slightly forward, 15 to 20 minutes. Cycling is better tolerated than walking when the canal is narrow.

dead.name: Core work in neutral
dead.how: Lying down, back in neutral, lift one knee then the other without moving the pelvis. 2 sets of 10.

ext.name: Sit tall
ext.how: Sitting on the edge of a chair, feet flat, hands on the thighs. Gently grow taller while opening the chest, hold 5 s. 10 times, without going into pain. After a recent fracture, wait for the doctor's agreement.
ext.videoSearch: seated posture extension osteoporosis exercise physiotherapy

chaise.name: Sit to stand
chaise.how: Without using your hands if possible, 3 sets of 8.
chaise.videoSearch: sit to stand strengthening older adults

rot.name: Lying trunk rotations
rot.how: Knees bent, let them drop to one side then the other. 10 times.
rot.videoSearch: lying lumbar rotation windscreen wiper exercise

respi.name: Deep breathing
respi.how: Breathe in while opening the ribs, 10 cycles, morning and evening.

questions.fesse: At the top of the buttock
